title: The angels
hookLine: created from light, obeying, never tiring

cards: Watch the end of any Muslim prayer. The person sitting on the floor turns the head to the right and says peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. Then to the left, the same words.
In a row, there's a person on each side, so the greeting lands somewhere.
But some scholars say it's meant for more than the neighbors: it's also for the angels, the ones the Qur'an describes as noble recorders, keeping watch over every person.
A small turn of the head, and a hello to the second article of faith.

teach.b: Day six hundred sixty-five met the angels by name; today, why they're an article of faith. Start with what they're made of.

A hadith in Sahih Muslim says the angels were created from light, the jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from what you have been told: the earth. Three kinds of creature, three materials. Next, what they do.
The Qur'an describes angels who carry out what they're commanded and do not disobey, and others who glorify Allah night and day without tiring.
Some are known by name and task: Jibril, who brought the revelation, Mika'il, and the angel of death. Others record, others guard. Then a surprise.
Obedient doesn't mean silent. In the second surah, Allah tells the angels, in Pickthall's translation, "Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth."
And the angels ask: will you put there someone who will do harm and shed blood, when we praise you?
Allah answers that He knows what they don't.
Adam is taught the names of things, and the angels admit they know only what they've been taught. The beings of light ask, and then they learn. Last, why believe in them at all.

For Muslims, angels are part of how the unseen world works: revelation came through one, deeds are written by others, and no deed goes unwitnessed. That's held not as a mood but as the second of the six.

how: Muslims end each prayer by turning the head right and left with the words peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah; belief in angels, including Jibril and the recording angels, is the second article of faith.

o: beings of light who obey God, record deeds and bring revelation
spirits made of smokeless fire, living unseen beside us
the souls of good people, raised up to heaven after they die

s: the angels were created from light
a hadith in Sahih Muslim says so, with the jinn from fire and Adam from earth.
in Surah al-Baqarah they ask why Allah would place on earth someone who will shed blood.
the turn of the head at the end of prayer is only for the people beside you
some scholars say the greeting is also for the angels.

games.q: you are one of the angels. Allah says, I am about to place a viceroy in the earth. what do you do?
o: ask: will you put there someone who will do harm and shed blood?
games.why: in Surah al-Baqarah the angels ask exactly that. Allah answers that He knows what they don't, and then Adam is taught the names.

practice: Settle, then turn your head gently to the right and say, aloud or inside, peace be upon you; turn to the left and say it again. Then face forward and stay there.
If you pray, this is the greeting you already know; if you don't, take it as a greeting to whatever company you keep, the people near you and whatever is unseen.

wordCard.voice: The angels. Mala'ikah in Arabic: created from light, obeying their Lord, glorifying Him without tiring. The second article of faith. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: angels; one angel is malak.

carryVoice: Your line: made of light. Tomorrow, the third article of faith: the books. See you tomorrow, then.

sources.q: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth
